neighbours.label: The word 'Twilight', tested in film-title, ordinary dusk, and word-mention contexts.
fire: The cinema club put Twilight on its autumn discussion list.
A borrowed copy of Twilight lay beside the television remote.
During the review, the critic compared Twilight with another vampire story.
My cousin chose Twilight for the final screening of the evening.
The last swallows crossed the valley in the twilight.
A narrow band of twilight remained above the western hills.
On the vocabulary sheet, the word Twilight was printed in blue.
The editor replaced the heading with the single word twilight.
quiet: For its autumn discussion, the cinema club selected Dracula.
Beside the television, we found a borrowed copy of Nosferatu.
A critic compared Interview with the Vampire to another supernatural story.
For the evening screening, my cousin picked a film called Daybreakers.
At dusk, the last swallows flew across the quiet valley.
Above the western hills, a narrow band of evening light remained.
The vocabulary sheet printed the word Daylight in blue letters.
A revised heading consisted of the single word sunset.

notes: The card is heterogeneous. Immune-system and hummingbird probes did not establish a clean common feature, while one Twilight title probe fired. This fresh test deliberately challenges a lexical interpretation with non-title uses. Even a hold would describe only a candidate sub-trigger.
